question: do reported earnings and cash reflect economic reality?

earnings_versus_cash.finding: Over the trailing four quarters operating cash flow is {earnings_versus_cash.operating_cash_flow_over_net_income} times net income and accruals over average assets are {earnings_versus_cash.accruals_over_average_assets|pct}: cash exceeds reported income. Against the company's own record that cover is below fiscal 2026 ({earnings_versus_cash.history.years.0.operating_cash_flow_over_net_income}) and above fiscal 2025 ({earnings_versus_cash.history.years.1.operating_cash_flow_over_net_income}); in six fiscal years only fiscal 2022 fell below one ({earnings_versus_cash.history.years.4.operating_cash_flow_over_net_income}). Annual accruals over total assets were {trend_table.years-back-0.ratios.accruals_over_total_assets|pct} in fiscal 2026 against {trend_table.years-back-1.ratios.accruals_over_total_assets|pct} in fiscal 2025, second lowest of five filled years. The quarter runs the other way. Quarterly accruals over total assets are {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.accruals_over_total_assets|pct}, positive and above the {trend_table.quarters-back-4.ratios.accruals_over_total_assets|pct} of the same quarter a year earlier; only two quarters are filled, so this is a comparison, not a trend. Net income grew {ratios.growth.net_income.year_over_year|pct} year over year against operating cash flow's {ratios.growth.operating_cash_flow.year_over_year|pct}; on the prior quarter net income changed by {ratios.growth.net_income.quarter_over_quarter|pct} and operating cash flow by {ratios.growth.operating_cash_flow.quarter_over_quarter|pct}. The notes explain part of the gap and the numbers bear it out: "the $46 million refund approved by CBP, but not yet received, was recorded as other current assets", and other current assets rose. Receivables rose within the quarter by {terms.trailing_four_quarters.change_in_receivables.parts.this_year_to_date.value} on the cash-flow statement against {terms.trailing_four_quarters.change_in_receivables.parts.prior_year_to_date.value} in the same quarter a year earlier, so that build is seasonal. Working capital is not absorbing earnings over the year: receivables rose {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.receivables.balance_sheet_change} year over year, {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.receivables.share_of_net_income|pct} of trailing net income; inventory changed by {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.inventory.balance_sheet_change} ({earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.inventory.share_of_net_income|pct}); payables rose {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.accounts_payable.balance_sheet_change} ({earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.accounts_payable.share_of_net_income|pct}); trade working capital went from {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_to_firm.trade_working_capital.a_year_earlier} to {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_to_firm.trade_working_capital.now}. Payables supplied less cash this quarter than a year earlier ({terms.trailing_four_quarters.change_in_payables.parts.this_year_to_date.value} against {terms.trailing_four_quarters.change_in_payables.parts.prior_year_to_date.value}), so the quarter leaned less on supplier credit, not more. Articulation: the balance-sheet and cash-flow-statement changes over the trailing year differ by {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.receivables.articulation_gap} for receivables, {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.inventory.articulation_gap} for inventory and {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.accounts_payable.articulation_gap} for payables, small against the flows and unexplained in my inputs. Separately, the cash-flow line for accrued and other liabilities shows an increase this quarter while the balance-sheet total of accrued and other current liabilities fell between March and June 2026; nothing in my inputs reconciles the two. Smoothness is {earnings_versus_cash.smoothness}, below one, so income moves less than cash. The December quarter's operating cash flow ({earnings_versus_cash.smoothness.operating_cash_flow.2}) far exceeds its net income ({earnings_versus_cash.smoothness.net_income.2}), the pattern of holiday collections, but no prose addresses it.
earnings_versus_cash.verdict: Earnings are backed by cash over the trailing year and in five of six fiscal years. This quarter income ran ahead of cash, in part because a one-time tariff refund was booked before it was collected.

revenue_recognition.finding: Receivables are not outrunning revenue this quarter. Days sales outstanding are {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.days_sales_outstanding} against {trend_table.quarters-back-4.ratios.days_sales_outstanding} a year earlier, third lowest of six filled quarters and below the high of {trend_table.quarters-back-3.ratios.days_sales_outstanding}. Receivables over quarterly revenue moved the same way ({trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.receivables_over_revenue} against {trend_table.quarters-back-4.ratios.receivables_over_revenue}), and trailing DSO on average balances is {ratios.efficiency.days_sales_outstanding}. That confirms MD&A's statement that DSO fell on the timing of sales and collections. At the fiscal 2026 year end, DSO rose to {trend_table.years-back-0.ratios.days_sales_outstanding} from {trend_table.years-back-1.ratios.days_sales_outstanding}. That is still second lowest of five filled years and below the fiscal 2023 high of {trend_table.years-back-3.ratios.days_sales_outstanding}, and no prose addresses the year-end rise. Contract liabilities moved toward deferral, not acceleration. Current contract liabilities over quarterly revenue are {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.contract_liabilities_over_revenue|pct}, the highest of six filled quarters, against {trend_table.quarters-back-4.ratios.contract_liabilities_over_revenue|pct} a year earlier. The balance went from {terms.balances_a_year_earlier.contract_liabilities} to {terms.balances_now.contract_liabilities}, the annual ratio is the highest of four filled years ({trend_table.years-back-0.ratios.contract_liabilities_over_revenue|pct}), and the non-current balance, which sits outside the ratio, also rose between March and June 2026. No prose explains the rise. The main judgment is variable consideration. Gross receivables are reduced by allowances for pricing programs, customer incentive programs and cooperative marketing, and each rose between March and June 2026 along with gross receivables. That matches MD&A's "partially offset by investment in strategic promotions". These allowances are tagged only by program type, so the calculator carries no allowance field and no ratio of allowance to gross receivables, and whether the reserves thinned cannot be stated here. My inputs show no change in revenue policy wording, no principal-versus-agent or standalone-selling-price change, no extended payment terms and no bill-and-hold; the policy paragraph still reports no material change. Fourth-quarter concentration: nothing found. The derived fiscal fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 carried revenue of {ratios.growth.revenue.quarter_over_quarter.inputs.before}, below this quarter's {ratios.growth.revenue.this_quarter} and below the year-earlier first quarter's {ratios.growth.revenue.year_over_year.inputs.before}; the seasonal peak is the December quarter, not the fiscal year end.
revenue_recognition.verdict: No sign of revenue pulled forward: receivables track sales and deferred revenue sits at a high. The sales-incentive allowances, the company's largest revenue judgment, rose with promotion spending, but the calculator cannot measure them against receivables.

estimates_and_reserves.finding: The quarter carries a one-time gain that rests on a recognition judgment. The notes say "The $61 million refund was recorded as a reduction of costs of goods sold" and add a new policy: "The Company recognizes tariff refunds when the gain is realized or realizable." Part of the gain was booked as an other current asset before the cash came in; MD&A says that cash arrived after quarter end, which supports realizability. The refund carries much of the profit growth. Operating income rose {ratios.growth.operating_income.year_over_year|pct} year over year on revenue growth of {ratios.growth.revenue.year_over_year|pct}, while the chief financial officer says "our operational performance was impressive even excluding these refunds, with non-GAAP operating income growing 14 percent year over year". MD&A also attributes most of the rise in interest income to the refund ("primarily driven by interest income associated with IEEPA tariff refunds"), and net income grew {ratios.growth.net_income.year_over_year|pct}, faster than operating income. The trailing operating margin of {ratios.profitability.operating_margin|pct} includes the refund; it compares with {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.0.operating_margin|pct} for fiscal 2026 and a three-year average of {earnings_versus_cash.history.operating_margin_three_year_average|pct}. The refund amount is not a field in calculator_filings_only.json, so no earnings adjustment can be written for it. A further refund may follow: temporary tariffs "were subsequently invalidated by the U.S. Court of International Trade, but remained in effect pending appeal", and the new policy would govern any recovery. Tax: the tagged quarterly effective rate fell against a year earlier. The notes attribute this to income mix and "higher tax benefits from share-based compensation", a discrete item tied to equity awards rather than operations. The trailing effective rate is {tax_rate.effective_rate|pct}, and the discrete amount is not in the calculator. Warranty: the accrual over quarterly revenue fell to {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.warranty_reserve_ratio|pct} from {trend_table.quarters-back-4.ratios.warranty_reserve_ratio|pct}, which was then the highest of six filled quarters. The balance went from {terms.balances_a_year_earlier.warranty_accrual} to {terms.balances_now.warranty_accrual} while revenue rose, and settlements exceeded new accruals for warranties issued in the quarter. The annual ratio slipped to {trend_table.years-back-0.ratios.warranty_reserve_ratio|pct} from {trend_table.years-back-1.ratios.warranty_reserve_ratio|pct}. The thinning is small and unexplained. Allowances: the bad-debt reserve ratio is filled in no period because the allowance is tagged only by program type. The company adopted a credit-loss practical expedient this quarter ("The Company adopted ASU 2025-05 in the first quarter of fiscal year 2027") and states no material impact, which cannot be tested. Inventory reserve: nothing is tagged in any period, inventory is tagged net of reserves, and no write-down is tagged. Goodwill: the notes reader lists no triggering event and no impairment, with dates rolled forward. No headroom, discount-rate or growth assumption is in my inputs, so nothing found. The tax-law and global minimum tax items are stated as de minimis and cannot be tested.
estimates_and_reserves.verdict: This quarter's earnings are lifted by a one-time tariff refund recognized on a realizable basis, by interest on that refund and by a discrete tax benefit. Warranty cover thinned modestly. The reserves that matter most here, the sales-incentive allowances and the inventory reserve, cannot be measured from the calculator.

cost_deferral.finding: No cost deferral found. No capitalized software or development cost is tagged in any period, so there is no comparison of capitalized against expensed cost. Research and development is expensed and rose ({terms.trailing_four_quarters.research_and_development_expense.parts.this_year_to_date.value} against {terms.trailing_four_quarters.research_and_development_expense.parts.prior_year_to_date.value}; trailing {terms.trailing_four_quarters.research_and_development_expense}). Capital expenditure is flat ({terms.trailing_four_quarters.capital_expenditure} against {terms.trailing_four_quarters_a_year_earlier.capital_expenditure}). Soft-asset share fell to {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.soft_asset_share|pct} from {trend_table.quarters-back-4.ratios.soft_asset_share|pct}, and the annual figure is the lowest of five filled years ({trend_table.years-back-0.ratios.soft_asset_share|pct}). One soft line did rise: prepaid expenses and other current assets went up between March and June 2026. The notes put the uncollected refund in other current assets without naming the line, so the rest of the rise is unexplained. Amortization of intangibles fell to {terms.trailing_four_quarters.depreciation_and_amortization.parts.this_year_to_date.parts.1.value} from {terms.trailing_four_quarters.depreciation_and_amortization.parts.prior_year_to_date.parts.1.value} because assets became fully amortized, as MD&A says. That lifts GAAP operating income with no operating change. Non-recurring items that recur: MD&A describes the restructuring plan as one "which was substantially completed in fiscal 2026", yet charges continue this quarter and are excluded from non-GAAP results; the amount is not in the calculator. Non-GAAP: the calculator holds no non-GAAP measure, so the gap's trend cannot be measured. The release excludes share-based compensation, amortization and restructuring but keeps the one-time refund inside its non-GAAP results: "These numbers include $61 million in tariff refunds." Non-GAAP operating income therefore overstates the recurring run rate this quarter.
cost_deferral.verdict: No costs are being pushed onto the balance sheet. The weakness in this area is presentation: non-GAAP results keep a one-time refund while removing recurring costs.

cash_flow_engineering_and_off_balance_sh.finding: Receivables factoring: nothing found. No proceeds from sale of receivables are tagged in any period, and no prose mentions factoring. Supplier finance: nothing found. No supplier-finance obligation is tagged, and no prose mentions a programme. Both are absences in the record, not confirmations from the filing. Purchase obligations and guarantees: neither is tagged. The notes reader lists MD&A's paragraph on inventory purchase commitments and the loss liability on them, and the paragraph on bank guarantees, as amounts only, so their size and movement are not in my inputs. Leases are on the balance sheet and falling ({terms.balances_a_year_earlier.operating_lease_liability} to {terms.balances_now.operating_lease_liability}); debt is {terms.debt_now}. Variable-interest entities: nothing in my inputs. Classification: no sign of shifting between operating and investing; capital expenditure is flat and there were no acquisitions. Timing: the uncollected refund came in after quarter end ("of which $15 million was received in cash within the quarter and $46 million was received subsequent to quarter end"). The next quarter's operating cash flow will therefore carry a one-time inflow that is not operating performance. Share-based compensation is a real cost: trailing {terms.trailing_four_quarters.share_based_compensation}, against {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.0.share_based_compensation} in fiscal 2026 and {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.1.share_based_compensation} in fiscal 2025. It is already subtracted, taking free cash flow from {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_simple} to {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_quality_adjusted}. Cash paid to withhold taxes on net share settlement rose sharply against a year earlier and sits in financing, outside free cash flow. Share-based compensation is already subtracted, so no further adjustment is written.
cash_flow_engineering_and_off_balance_sh.verdict: No cash-flow engineering is visible, though the absence of factoring and supplier-finance tags is a gap, not proof. Next quarter's operating cash flow will include a one-time refund collection.

controls_audit_and_filing_signals.finding: The current window is clean. The controls item of the 10-Q still concludes that disclosure controls are effective and reports no change in internal control. As a 10-Q it carries no auditor's report and no critical audit matters. Since the prior 10-Q, "There is no 4.01, 4.02, 5.02 or NT filing in that window." That means no auditor change, no officer-departure filing and no late filing. The release was labeled preliminary, and the 10-Q filed the next day carries the same headline figures. Older record: "They list an item 3.01 filing on 2025-10-02, an item 4.02 filing on 2014-09-04, an item 4.01 filing on 2014-11-13, and four NT 10-K/10-Q notices from 2014 to 2015." The 2014 non-reliance filing, the 2014 auditor change and the late-filing notices of 2014 and 2015 are more than a decade old, but they show the company has withdrawn reliance on its own statements before. The 2025 filing falls under the item that covers delisting notices or a transfer of listing, and its content is not in my inputs. Quiet restatement cannot be checked: no restatement trace is in my inputs, and the trend table takes prior-period values from later filings without a flag. Related parties, the subsidiary list and SEC comment letters are not in my inputs. The Chief Legal Officer adopted a pre-arranged plan to sell shares, which has no accounting bearing.
controls_audit_and_filing_signals.verdict: Clean in the current window. The record holds a non-reliance filing and an auditor change from 2014, and a recent listing-related filing whose content I cannot see.

cross_document_reconciliation.finding: The 8-K release matches the 10-Q. On every headline line the numbers reader set side by side (net sales, gross profit, operating income, net income, receivables, cash and operating cash flow, both years) the figures agree, and no adjustment between the preliminary release and the filing is visible. The numbers confirm these notes items: the receivables build on sales and timing, the fall in DSO, the rise in payables, the rise in working capital and other current assets, the rise in promotion and incentive allowances, the fall in the effective tax rate, the fall in intangible amortization, the rise in operating income with the refund inside it, sales growth this quarter, the EMEA decline, the tablet decline, the pointing-device rise and the release's repurchase cash figure. One item is contradicted. The notes paragraph naming component availability, energy prices and the Middle East conflict points net sales down this quarter, but total net sales rose {ratios.growth.revenue.year_over_year|pct} year over year and {ratios.growth.revenue.quarter_over_quarter|pct} on the prior quarter; only EMEA declined. Unresolved are the forward items (supplier incident, new tariffs, dividend, next-quarter outlook), the refund interest, the cost-of-goods-sold line itself, days payable and inventory turnover (the record has no cost-of-revenue row), restructuring, and the completed-program question. Three document gaps stand. First, the supplier incident is sized only in the release ("For Q3, based on limited available information, the negative impact of the supplier incident is estimated to be up to $200 million in net sales."), and the 10-Q gives no amount. Second, the gross margin ("GAAP gross margin was 49.5 percent, up 780 basis points, compared to Q1 of the prior year.") exists only in the release, because the 10-Q record tags gross profit but no cost of goods sold. Third, the notes say "The 2023 share repurchase program was completed in May 2026.", yet that program's row shows no repurchases this quarter, and cash paid for repurchases ({terms.trailing_four_quarters.share_repurchases.parts.this_year_to_date.value}) exceeds the cost recorded under the new program.
cross_document_reconciliation.verdict: The release and the 10-Q agree on every headline figure. One notes claim runs against reported total sales, and the supplier-incident size and the gross margin appear only in the release.

industry_lens.finding: Inventory obsolescence: nothing found, though the reserve cannot be measured. No inventory reserve or write-down is tagged in any period, and days of inventory cannot be computed for lack of a cost-of-revenue row. Inventory changed by {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.inventory.balance_sheet_change} year over year (now {terms.balances_now.inventory} against {terms.balances_a_year_earlier.inventory}) and barely moved within the quarter while sales grew, so there is no build. The new risk runs the other way. The notes now say the company has been hit by component demand "leading to shortages and rising prices for such components", and a semiconductor supplier's facility closed. Purchase commitments in excess of need: nothing found in the numbers. No purchase obligation is tagged, and the MD&A paragraph on purchase commitments and the loss liability on them is listed as amounts only. Commitments signed at shortage prices are a forward risk. Customer concentration: three customers are disclosed individually. In fiscal 2026, customers A, B and C held {concentration.facts.26.value|pct}, {concentration.facts.27.value|pct} and {concentration.facts.28.value|pct} of revenue, little changed from fiscal 2025 ({concentration.facts.13.value|pct}, {concentration.facts.14.value|pct}, {concentration.facts.15.value|pct}). Their shares of receivables at year end rose for all three: A from {concentration.facts.16.value|pct} to {concentration.facts.29.value|pct}, B from {concentration.facts.17.value|pct} to {concentration.facts.30.value|pct}, C from {concentration.facts.18.value|pct} to {concentration.facts.31.value|pct}. Receivables are concentrating in the largest customers while their revenue shares hold still. No prose explains it, and no quarter-level customer fact is in the calculator. Channel stuffing: no sign this quarter. DSO fell, inventory is flat and the fiscal fourth quarter is not the peak. Worth watching are the rising incentive and pricing allowances, the higher year-end DSO and the receivable concentration. Circular or vendor-financed deals: nothing found. The company holds equity-method and other investments, listed as amounts only with no impairment, but nothing in my inputs links them to customers.
industry_lens.verdict: No obsolescence or channel build is visible. The open risks are receivables concentrating in the three largest customers and supply-side commitments made during a component shortage.

The December quarter's operating cash flow of {earnings_versus_cash.smoothness.operating_cash_flow.2} far exceeds its net income of {earnings_versus_cash.smoothness.net_income.2}, consistent with holiday collections. No prose addresses it.

anomalies.name: Small working-capital articulation gaps
anomalies.name_ko: 운전자본 변동의 재무상태표·현금흐름표 간 소폭 불일치
anomalies.what: Over the trailing year, balance-sheet changes and cash-flow-statement changes differ by {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.receivables.articulation_gap} for receivables, {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.inventory.articulation_gap} for inventory and {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.accounts_payable.articulation_gap} for payables. The gaps are small against the flows, and nothing in my inputs explains them.

anomalies.name: Accrued-liabilities cash line rose while the balance fell
anomalies.name_ko: 미지급비용 현금흐름 항목은 증가, 재무상태표 잔액은 감소
anomalies.what: The cash-flow line for accrued and other liabilities shows an increase this quarter. Over the same months, the balance-sheet total of accrued and other current liabilities fell between March and June 2026, with employee-related and other accrued liabilities both lower. Nothing in my inputs reconciles the two.

anomalies.name: Payables supplied less operating cash than a year earlier
anomalies.name_ko: 매입채무가 공급한 현금이 전년보다 적음
anomalies.what: Payables supplied {terms.trailing_four_quarters.change_in_payables.parts.this_year_to_date.value} of operating cash this quarter, against {terms.trailing_four_quarters.change_in_payables.parts.prior_year_to_date.value} a year earlier. MD&A says payables rose on inventory purchases and timing, which the balance confirms, but the smaller inflow against last year is not explained. It means less reliance on supplier credit, not more.

anomalies.name: Contract liabilities at their highest share of revenue
anomalies.name_ko: 계약부채의 매출 대비 비율이 최고 수준
anomalies.what: Current contract liabilities over quarterly revenue are {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.contract_liabilities_over_revenue|pct}, the highest of six filled quarters, against {trend_table.quarters-back-4.ratios.contract_liabilities_over_revenue|pct} a year earlier. The annual ratio, {trend_table.years-back-0.ratios.contract_liabilities_over_revenue|pct}, is the highest of four filled years, against {trend_table.years-back-1.ratios.contract_liabilities_over_revenue|pct}. The balance went from {terms.balances_a_year_earlier.contract_liabilities} to {terms.balances_now.contract_liabilities}. Deferral is the conservative direction, but no prose explains the rise.

anomalies.name: Fiscal year-end receivables rose against revenue
anomalies.name_ko: 회계연도 말 매출채권 회수기간 상승
anomalies.what: At the fiscal 2026 year end, DSO was {trend_table.years-back-0.ratios.days_sales_outstanding} against {trend_table.years-back-1.ratios.days_sales_outstanding} a year earlier, and receivables over revenue were {trend_table.years-back-0.ratios.receivables_over_revenue} against {trend_table.years-back-1.ratios.receivables_over_revenue}. Both are still second lowest of five filled years. The current quarter's DSO fell. No prose addresses the year-end rise.

anomalies.name: Pricing, incentive and marketing allowances rising
anomalies.name_ko: 가격·판매장려·공동마케팅 충당금 증가
anomalies.what: Allowances for pricing programs, customer incentive programs and cooperative marketing all rose between March and June 2026, together with gross receivables, and MD&A names investment in strategic promotions. These variable-consideration reserves are tagged by program type only, so the calculator holds no allowance field and no ratio to gross receivables.

anomalies.name: One-time tariff refund booked as a cost reduction
anomalies.name_ko: 일회성 관세 환급을 매출원가 감소로 처리
anomalies.what: A refund of invalidated tariffs was booked as a reduction of cost of goods sold. Operating income rose {ratios.growth.operating_income.year_over_year|pct} on revenue growth of {ratios.growth.revenue.year_over_year|pct}, while the chief financial officer says underlying non-GAAP operating income grew far less. The refund amount is not a calculator field, so no adjustment is written.

anomalies.name: Refund gain recognized before cash was received
anomalies.name_ko: 현금 수령 전 환급 이익 인식
anomalies.what: Part of the refund was recognized as an other current asset before cash came in, under a new realized-or-realizable policy, and other current assets rose. MD&A says the cash came after quarter end, which supports the recognition.

anomalies.name: Interest income lifted by refund interest
anomalies.name_ko: 환급금 이자로 이자수익 증가
anomalies.what: MD&A attributes the higher interest income mainly to interest on the refunds, a non-recurring source whose amount is not in the calculator. Net income grew {ratios.growth.net_income.year_over_year|pct}, more than operating income's {ratios.growth.operating_income.year_over_year|pct}.

anomalies.name: Tax rate lowered by share-based compensation benefits
anomalies.name_ko: 주식보상 세금 혜택으로 실효세율 하락
anomalies.what: The tagged quarterly effective rate fell against a year earlier. The notes attribute this in part to higher tax benefits from share-based compensation, a discrete item. The trailing rate is {tax_rate.effective_rate|pct}. Cash withheld on share settlements rose sharply, consistent with more vesting.

anomalies.name: Warranty reserve thinning against revenue
anomalies.name_ko: 매출 대비 제품보증충당금 감소
anomalies.what: The warranty accrual over quarterly revenue is {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.warranty_reserve_ratio|pct}, against {trend_table.quarters-back-4.ratios.warranty_reserve_ratio|pct} a year earlier. The balance went from {terms.balances_a_year_earlier.warranty_accrual} to {terms.balances_now.warranty_accrual} while revenue rose, and settlements exceeded new accruals for warranties issued in the quarter. The annual ratio is {trend_table.years-back-0.ratios.warranty_reserve_ratio|pct}, against {trend_table.years-back-1.ratios.warranty_reserve_ratio|pct}. No prose explains it.

anomalies.name: Credit-loss expedient adopted on an allowance that cannot be measured
anomalies.name_ko: 측정 불가한 대손충당금에 실무적 간편법 채택
anomalies.what: The company adopted a credit-loss practical expedient this quarter and states no material impact. The allowance is tagged only by program type, so the bad-debt reserve ratio is filled in no period and the claim cannot be tested.

anomalies.name: A further tariff refund could create another one-time gain
anomalies.name_ko: 추가 관세 환급에 따른 일회성 이익 가능성
anomalies.what: Temporary tariffs were invalidated but remain in effect pending appeal. The new policy recognizes a refund when it is realized or realizable, so another non-recurring credit to cost of goods sold may follow. The notes do not say whether the company paid those tariffs.

anomalies.name: Non-GAAP results keep a one-time refund
anomalies.name_ko: 비GAAP 실적에 일회성 환급 포함
anomalies.what: The release's non-GAAP results exclude share-based compensation, amortization and restructuring but keep the one-time tariff refund. The calculator has no non-GAAP measure, so the trend in the gap cannot be measured.

anomalies.name: Restructuring charges continue after the plan was called complete
anomalies.name_ko: 완료되었다는 구조조정 비용이 계속 발생
anomalies.what: MD&A says the plan was substantially completed in fiscal 2026, yet charges continue this quarter and are excluded from non-GAAP results. The amount is not in the calculator.

anomalies.name: Prepaid and other current assets rising
anomalies.name_ko: 선급비용 및 기타유동자산 증가
anomalies.what: Prepaid expenses and other current assets rose between March and June 2026, while the overall soft-asset share fell to {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.soft_asset_share|pct}. The notes place the uncollected refund in other current assets without naming the line, so the rest of the rise is unexplained.

anomalies.name: Intangible amortization falling as assets run off
anomalies.name_ko: 무형자산 상각 종료로 상각비 감소
anomalies.what: Amortization of intangibles fell to {terms.trailing_four_quarters.depreciation_and_amortization.parts.this_year_to_date.parts.1.value} from {terms.trailing_four_quarters.depreciation_and_amortization.parts.prior_year_to_date.parts.1.value} as assets became fully amortized. That lifts GAAP operating income with no operating change.

anomalies.name: One-time refund cash will lift next quarter's operating cash flow
anomalies.name_ko: 다음 분기 영업현금흐름에 일회성 환급 현금 유입
anomalies.what: The uncollected part of the refund was received after quarter end. Next quarter's operating cash flow will therefore include a one-time inflow that does not reflect operating performance. The amount is not in the calculator.

anomalies.name: Cash withheld on share settlements rising, outside free cash flow
anomalies.name_ko: 주식 순결제 원천징수 현금 증가(잉여현금흐름 밖)
anomalies.what: Cash paid to withhold taxes on net share settlement rose sharply against a year earlier and is classified in financing, outside free cash flow. Share-based compensation of {terms.trailing_four_quarters.share_based_compensation} is already subtracted in {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_quality_adjusted}, so no further adjustment is written.

anomalies.name: Past non-reliance filing, auditor change and late-filing notices
anomalies.name_ko: 과거 재무제표 신뢰 철회 공시·감사인 교체·지연 제출 통지
anomalies.what: The 8-K item index lists a non-reliance filing and an auditor change in 2014, and late-filing notices in 2014 and 2015. None falls in the current window. The index carries no paragraph id, so no item exists to cite.

anomalies.name: Recent filing under the delisting-or-transfer item
anomalies.name_ko: 최근 상장 관련 항목 공시
anomalies.what: The 8-K item index lists a 2025 filing under the item that covers delisting notices or a transfer of listing. Its content is not in my inputs.

anomalies.name: Notes point sales down; total sales rose
anomalies.name_ko: 주석은 매출 감소를 시사하나 전체 매출은 증가
anomalies.what: The notes list component availability, energy prices and the Middle East conflict among conditions pointing net sales down this quarter. Total net sales rose {ratios.growth.revenue.year_over_year|pct} year over year; only EMEA declined.

anomalies.name: Supplier incident sized only in the earnings release
anomalies.name_ko: 공급업체 사고 규모는 실적 발표문에만 기재
anomalies.what: The release sizes the supplier incident's effect on next-quarter and third-quarter net sales and mentions mitigation plans. The 10-Q describes the closure but gives no amount.

anomalies.name: Gross margin exists only in the release
anomalies.name_ko: 매출총이익률은 발표문에만 존재
anomalies.what: The release prints a GAAP gross margin and its rise, and MD&A explains days payable and inventory turnover through the refund's effect on cost of goods sold. The 10-Q record tags gross profit but no cost of goods sold in any period, so none of these can be checked.

anomalies.name: Repurchase program called complete with no quarter activity
anomalies.name_ko: 분기 중 매입 없이 완료되었다는 자사주 매입 프로그램
anomalies.what: The notes say the earlier program was completed in May 2026, but its row shows no repurchases this quarter. Cash paid for repurchases, {terms.trailing_four_quarters.share_repurchases.parts.this_year_to_date.value}, exceeds the cost recorded under the new program, part of that cost was unpaid at quarter end, and the treasury share count moved down. Nothing reconciles these.

anomalies.name: Receivables concentrating in the three largest customers
anomalies.name_ko: 상위 세 고객으로 매출채권 집중 심화
anomalies.what: At the fiscal 2026 year end, the receivable shares of customers A, B and C rose: A from {concentration.facts.16.value|pct} to {concentration.facts.29.value|pct}, B from {concentration.facts.17.value|pct} to {concentration.facts.30.value|pct}, C from {concentration.facts.18.value|pct} to {concentration.facts.31.value|pct}. Their revenue shares held near {concentration.facts.26.value|pct}, {concentration.facts.27.value|pct} and {concentration.facts.28.value|pct}. No prose explains it.

anomalies.name: Component shortage and supplier closure with no reserve or commitment data
anomalies.name_ko: 부품 부족·공급업체 폐쇄, 재고충당금·구매약정 수치 없음
anomalies.what: The notes now say component shortages have affected the company and that a semiconductor supplier's facility closed. Inventory stands at {terms.balances_now.inventory}, against {terms.balances_a_year_earlier.inventory} a year earlier. No inventory reserve, write-down or purchase obligation is tagged, so the effect on reserves and commitments cannot be measured.

summary_ko.earnings_versus_cash: 최근 네 분기 동안 영업현금흐름은 순이익의 {earnings_versus_cash.operating_cash_flow_over_net_income}배로 이익을 충분히 뒷받침하지만, 이번 분기에는 순이익이 현금보다 앞섰습니다(분기 발생액 비율 {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.accruals_over_total_assets|pct}, 전년 같은 분기 {trend_table.quarters-back-4.ratios.accruals_over_total_assets|pct}). 그 일부는 아직 받지 않은 관세 환급금을 기타유동자산으로 잡아 이익에 먼저 반영했기 때문입니다.
summary_ko.revenue_recognition: 이번 분기 매출채권 회수기간은 {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.days_sales_outstanding}일로 전년 같은 분기의 {trend_table.quarters-back-4.ratios.days_sales_outstanding}일보다 짧아, 매출을 앞당겨 인식한 흔적은 없습니다. 다만 가격·판매장려 충당금이 늘었고 계약부채 비율은 여섯 분기 중 가장 높은데, 충당금 비율은 계산기에 없어 확인할 수 없습니다.
summary_ko.estimates_and_reserves: 영업이익은 전년 대비 {ratios.growth.operating_income.year_over_year|pct} 늘었지만, 상당 부분은 무효화된 관세의 일회성 환급을 매출원가 감소로 처리한 결과입니다. 환급액은 계산기 항목에 없어 조정하지 못했습니다. 주식보상 세금 혜택으로 실효세율도 낮아졌고, 보증충당금 비율은 {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.warranty_reserve_ratio|pct}로 전년의 {trend_table.quarters-back-4.ratios.warranty_reserve_ratio|pct}보다 다소 얇아졌습니다.
summary_ko.cost_deferral: 소프트웨어나 개발비를 자산으로 이연한 흔적은 없으며, 연구개발비는 모두 비용 처리되었고 늘었습니다. 다만 회사의 비GAAP 실적은 주식보상·상각·구조조정 비용은 빼면서 일회성 관세 환급은 그대로 포함해, 반복 이익을 실제보다 크게 보이게 합니다.
summary_ko.cash_flow_engineering_and_off_balance_sh: 매출채권 매각, 공급망 금융, 차입금은 기록에 없고 리스부채는 줄었습니다. 분기 말 이후 들어온 관세 환급 현금은 다음 분기 영업현금흐름에 일회성 유입으로 잡힐 것이며, 주식보상 {terms.trailing_four_quarters.share_based_compensation}는 품질조정 잉여현금흐름에서 이미 차감했습니다.
summary_ko.controls_audit_and_filing_signals: 이번 기간에는 감사인 교체, 재무 책임자 이탈 공시, 지연 제출이 없고 공시통제도 유효하다고 보고했습니다. 다만 2014년의 재무제표 신뢰 철회 공시와 감사인 교체, 그리고 내용이 입력에 없는 2025년 상장 관련 공시가 기록에 남아 있습니다.
summary_ko.cross_document_reconciliation: 8-K 실적 발표와 10-Q의 핵심 수치는 모두 일치합니다. 다만 중동 분쟁 등으로 매출이 줄어든다는 주석 문장은 전체 매출이 {ratios.growth.revenue.year_over_year|pct} 늘어난 숫자와 어긋나고, 공급업체 사고의 규모와 매출총이익률은 발표문에만 나옵니다.
summary_ko.industry_lens: 재고는 쌓이지 않았고 회계연도 마지막 분기에 매출이 몰리지도 않았습니다. 그러나 상위 세 고객의 매출채권 비중이 모두 높아졌고(고객 B는 {concentration.facts.17.value|pct}에서 {concentration.facts.30.value|pct}로), 부품 부족과 공급업체 공장 폐쇄로 구매약정 위험이 커졌지만 관련 수치는 기록에 없습니다.

limits: This analysis finds where the numbers and the explanations disagree, and where the company differs from its own past. It does not judge intent, and it cannot see evidence outside the filings, such as invoices or contracts.
